faq.q: Which colour formats can I type in and get back?
faq.a: You can enter a hex (3, 6 or 8 digit), rgb/rgba, hsl/hsla, hsv, cmyk or a CSS colour name, and it converts to all of them at once — HEX, HEX8 with alpha, RGB, RGBA, HSL, HSLA, HSV, CMYK and the nearest named colour. Internally it works in HSV with an alpha channel, and there's a visual saturation/value square, hue bar and alpha bar.

faq.q: What colour harmonies does it generate?
faq.a: Complementary, analogous (±30°), triadic (120° apart), tetradic (90° apart), split-complementary and monochromatic. Each is computed by rotating the hue around the wheel and rendered as clickable swatches you can copy. The deep notes explain what each harmony is actually useful for.

faq.q: How does the tint and shade scale work?
faq.a: It produces a ten-step scale labelled 50–900 by holding your colour's hue and saturation and varying the HSL lightness. The label text colour on each swatch is chosen by WCAG relative luminance (the 0.179 crossover), not raw lightness, so numbers stay readable even on bright mid-tones. Clicking any step copies its hex.

faq.q: Can I check contrast and export the palette?
faq.a: Yes. The built-in contrast checker shows your colour's ratio on white, on black and on a custom background, flagging AA and AAA for normal and large text. There's an Eyedropper (where the browser's EyeDropper API is supported, e.g. Chrome/Edge desktop). Export the generated scale as CSS variables, SCSS, Tailwind config or JSON, and saved/recent colours persist in your browser.
